All panels except (a) are produced by
[`script/Figure6.R`](https://github.com/AgueroZZ/immgenT-GP-analysis/blob/main/script/Figure6.R),
which shares its CITE-seq setup with [Figure S6](FigureS6.html) via
`code/R/citeseq_shared_setup.R`. The code below is shown for
reference (not re-executed on this page, since this script takes about a
minute to run); the images are its pre-rendered output.

**Panel order changed on 2026-07-28.** The figure was reordered and two panels
moved out to [Figure S6](FigureS6.html), so the letters here no longer match the
published figure: the KLRG1 and CD69 panels moved to the front (published g, h,
i are now b, c, d), the four gating panels moved back (published c-f are now
e-h), and two new gating panels were added, (i) GP77 and (j) GP8. The published
protein-program heatmap 6b is now [Fig. S6a](FigureS6.html#figs6a), and the
published 6j/6k are now [Fig. S6b, c](FigureS6.html#figs6bc). `script/Figure6.R`
carries the full old-to-new table in its header.

## (a) Protein-signature schematic {#fig6a}

This panel is a hand-drawn schematic, not generated from R -- there is no code or pre-rendered image to show here. See `figures/Previous/bits/Figure 6/6a.pdf` for the published panel.

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6a.** Schematic illustrating how protein signatures were defined for each
GP. Holding the cell-loading matrix **L** fixed from the GP model, a protein
factor matrix was estimated by EBMF from the paired CITE-seq protein
measurements, Y ≈ LUᵀ (cells × proteins matrix), yielding a protein signature
**U** (proteins × GPs matrix) for each GP. See
[Methods: fitting CITE-seq protein programs with fixed scRNA loadings](Methods_FlashierFit_Citeseq.html).
:::

## (b, c) KLRG1 modulation across lineages {#fig6bc}

```{r fig6bc-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6b"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6bc-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="49%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("assets/Figure6/6b.png", "assets/Figure6/6c.png"))
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6b, c.** GPs associated with KLRG1 protein expression in CD4, Tregs and CD8. Within each lineage, cells are split KLRG1+ versus KLRG1- based on the threshold on the KLRG1 protein, and for every GP the effect size is the difference in its mean activity between KLRG1+ and KLRG1- cells. These effect-size versus effect-size plots compare CD8+ T cells (x-axis) with CD4+ T cells (b) or Treg cells (c) (y-axis); each point is a GP, the dashed red line marks equal effect (y = x), and the dashed blue lines mark zero. Selected GPs are labeled -- orange for large, concordant effects in both lineages, and blue/pink for lineage-biased GPs.
:::

## (d) Genes up- and down-regulated across the CD69-associated GPs {#fig6d}

The ten GPs, and the correlation-based order they are drawn in, are defined once
in `code/R/citeseq_shared_setup.R`, because
[Fig. S6b, c](FigureS6.html#figs6bc) show the same GPs in the same order from a
different script:

```{r fig6d-gps, code=code_for("../code/R/citeseq_shared_setup.R", "doc:cd69"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6d-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6d"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6d-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure6/6d.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6d.** GPs associated with CD69 protein expression. Heatmap of the genes
most strongly **up- and down-regulated** across ten representative
CD69-associated GPs, ordered by the Spearman correlation between GP activity and
CD69 expression, with the left strip indicating that correlation
(blue-white-red). The genes shown are, per GP, its top five positively and top
five negatively scoring genes, then restricted to those reaching |score| >= 0.5
in at least one of the ten (green-white-purple). Mean activity of the same ten
GPs across tissues and lineages is shown in
[Fig. S6b, c](FigureS6.html#figs6bc) (published as Extended Data Figure 6b, c).

The ten GPs are a **hand-picked** set drawn from among the GPs most strongly
correlated -- positively or negatively -- with CD69, not a computed top-10:
eight are positively correlated (ranks 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12 and 14 of 200) and
GP58/GP171 are the two most *negatively* correlated GPs of all 200.
`script/verify_cd69_gp_ranking.R` recomputes the correlation over all 200 GPs and
fails if this wording and the code drift apart.
:::

## (e-j) Protein-gated vs. GP-loading populations {#fig6ej}

```{r fig6ej-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6e"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6ej-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="49%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c(
  "assets/Figure6/6e.png", "assets/Figure6/6f.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6g.png", "assets/Figure6/6h.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6i.png", "assets/Figure6/6j.png"
))
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6e-j.** Examples of gating strategies used to identify GP-active cells, for
**(e) GP171, (f) GP12, (g) GP80, (h) GP23, (i) GP77 and (j) GP8**. For each GP,
cells are shown twice on the same MDE embedding. Left, cells selected by the
proposed protein gate, built from the GP's curated marker signature (positive
markers above, and negative markers below), with the gate size reported in the
panel title as "Matched n"; right, an equally sized set of cells with the
highest GP activity -- exactly as many cells as the protein gate selected. Color
indicates cell density (two-dimensional); all other cells are grey. Thymocytes,
proliferating, and "miniverse" cells are excluded. Four further GPs are gated the
same way in [Fig. S6d-g](FigureS6.html#figs6dg) (published as Extended Data
Figure 6d-g).
:::
